items.title: Chile's Kast fires security minister in first cabinet shake-up

featured_image.name: Kast Sacks Security Minister Two Months Into His Administration - Bloomberg

items.description: Chilean President José Antonio Kast carried out his first cabinet reshuffle on Tuesday, removing Security Minister Trinidad Steinert and Government Spokesperson Mara Sedini just over two months into his administration, in a shake-up that underscores growing unease over his government's handling of its core policy promise: fighting crime.[1][2][3]

items.title: NATO weighs Hormuz mission as top commander confirms talks

featured_image.name: NATO Is Starting to Consider Hormuz Deployment to Protect Ships

items.description: NATO is actively discussing the possibility of deploying a military mission to the Strait of Hormuz if the critical waterway remains blocked beyond early July, according to Bloomberg reporting confirmed by alliance officials. The deliberations mark a potential turning point for the alliance, which has so far avoided direct involvement in the broader U.S.-Iran conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Outbreak of highly contagious infection grows to more than 220 cases
items.description: Federal and state governments have mobilised to address the largest outbreak of diphtheria in recent memory, with the Commonwealth preparing a support package for a disease once considered almost eradicated.

items.title: EU reaches deal to cut US import duties ahead of Trump's tariff deadline

featured_image.name: EU prepares to cut US import duties to avoid Trump tariff hike | Reuters

items.description:
European Union negotiators reached a provisional agreement early Wednesday on legislation to eliminate import duties on US goods, clearing a critical hurdle in the bloc's race to comply with President Donald Trump's July 4 ultimatum before tariffs on European exports escalate sharply.

The deal, struck after a final round of trilogue talks between the European Parliament and the Council of the EU in Strasbourg, finalizes the legislative framework needed to implement the Turnberry Agreement — the trade pact reached between Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025.[1][2]

items.title: Drone strike kills 28 at crowded market in Sudan

featured_image.name: Drone attack on busy market in Sudan kills at least 28 - Al Jazeera

items.description:
A drone strike hit a bustling market in the town of Ghabesh in Sudan's West Kordofan state on Tuesday, killing at least 28 people and wounding dozens more, according to local rights monitors.[1][2][3]

The attack, reported by the Emergency Lawyers group, marks the latest in a relentless wave of drone warfare against civilian targets in Sudan's Kordofan region, where fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has intensified in recent months.[2][4]

items.title: Trump's Gaza board warns of funding gap in UN report

featured_image.name: Trump's Gaza board reports funding 'gap', urges quicker disbursement |  Reuters

items.description:
President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has warned that the gap between funding pledges and actual disbursements for Gaza's reconstruction must be closed "with urgency," according to a May 15 report to the United Nations Security Council viewed by Reuters on Tuesday.[1][2]

The board, established to oversee Trump's plan to rebuild the war-shattered territory, said that funds committed but not yet disbursed represent "the difference between a framework that exists on paper and one that delivers on the ground for the people of Gaza". While the report confirmed that $17 billion remains pledged, it did not disclose how much has actually been received or quantify the shortfall.[3][2]

items.title: NATO has no Hormuz mission plans, top commander says

featured_image.name: NATO not drawing up plans for Hormuz mission, top commander says | Reuters

items.description: NATO's top military commander said Tuesday that the alliance has no plans in motion for an operation in the Strait of Hormuz, underscoring that any such mission would first require political consensus among all 32 member states — a threshold that remains far from being met.

items.title: Trump says US may strike Iran again within days

featured_image.name: Trump reiterates Iran nuclear talking points despite swirling questions

items.description: President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that the United States may need to attack Iran again, revealing he was just an hour away from ordering a new strike before he postponed the operation. The remarks came a day after Trump called off what he described as a "very major attack" that had been scheduled for Tuesday, at the request of Gulf allies who said diplomatic negotiations were making progress.

items.title: NATO weighs naval mission in Hormuz as strait nears four months of closure

featured_image.name: Countries to Meet on Hormuz Naval Mission Led by UK, France

items.description: NATO is actively discussing a potential naval deployment to help secure commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz if the waterway remains blocked into early July, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, citing a senior alliance official. The discussions mark a shift for the alliance, which earlier this year refused to participate in the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports but now faces mounting pressure as the disruption to one of the world's most critical shipping routes approaches its fourth month.[1]

items.title: Google I/O 2026 kicks off today with Gemini AI updates

featured_image.name: Google I/O 2026 starts tomorrow: How to watch and what to expect ...

items.description: Google is rolling out a slate of updates to its Gemini AI assistant just as Google I/O 2026 kicks off today, May 19, at Shoreline Amphitheatre in Mountain View, California. Among the most notable additions is a "thinking level" control that lets users choose how much reasoning the model applies to their prompts — addressing a longstanding complaint about fixed reasoning modes.

items.title: Russia claims Ukraine plans drone strikes from Latvia, threatens Riga

featured_image.name: Russia's foreign intelligence service claims Ukraine preparing drone ...

items.description:
Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) claimed on Monday that Ukraine is preparing to launch drone strikes against Russian targets from Latvian military bases, an accusation swiftly rejected by both Riga and Kyiv as disinformation.

The SVR alleged that soldiers from Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces had already been deployed to military installations in Latvia, and that Kyiv intended to use Latvian territory — not just airspace — as a launching platform for attacks, calculating that shorter flight distances would increase the effectiveness of strikes. The agency added a veiled threat, stating that "the coordinates of decision-making centers on Latvian territory are well known" and that NATO membership "will not protect those who aid terrorists from just retribution".[1][2]
